concepts.name: type-feedback-and-speculation
concepts.description: TurboFan uses runtime type feedback to speculate on input types and generate fast specialized code with guards.

concepts.name: hidden-class
concepts.description: A hidden description of an object's layout that maps property names to offsets for fast access.

concepts.name: inline-cache
concepts.description: A cache at each property access site that remembers hidden classes and offsets to speed up property reads.

concepts.name: shape-transition
concepts.description: The process of moving an object from one hidden class to another when a property is added.

concepts.name: mark-sweep-compact
concepts.description: The major garbage collection algorithm that marks live objects, sweeps dead ones, and compacts memory to reduce fragmentation.

concepts.name: scavenger
concepts.description: The minor garbage collector that quickly cleans the young generation by copying live objects between semi-spaces.

concepts.name: v8-heap-layout
concepts.description: V8 heap is divided into spaces like young and old generations to manage objects with different lifetimes efficiently.

concepts.name: write-barrier
concepts.description: A mechanism that tracks pointers from old to young objects to ensure correct minor garbage collection.

concepts.name: deoptimization-triggers
concepts.description: Common reasons optimized code falls back to interpreter, such as type changes, shape changes, and insufficient feedback.

concepts.name: monomorphic-code
concepts.description: Code where call sites or property accesses see only one type or shape, enabling better optimization.

concepts.name: polymorphic-code
concepts.description: Code where call sites or property accesses see a few types or shapes, allowing some optimization but less than monomorphic.

concepts.name: v8-sampling-profiler
concepts.description: A tool enabled by --prof that samples program execution to identify hot functions and performance bottlenecks.

concepts.name: long-polling
concepts.description: Client sends a request that the server holds open until data is available or timeout occurs.

concepts.name: polling
concepts.description: Client repeatedly requests updates at intervals, causing latency and wasted server work.

concepts.name: push-based-communication
concepts.description: Communication where the server initiates sending data to the client without waiting for client requests.

concepts.name: real-time-system
concepts.description: A system where the server can push updates to the client immediately without client requests.

concepts.name: websockets
concepts.description: A persistent, full-duplex connection upgrading HTTP to allow low-latency, low-overhead server-client messaging.

concepts.name: tcp-stream
concepts.description: TCP provides a reliable, ordered, bidirectional stream of bytes without message boundaries.

concepts.name: websocket-frame-format
concepts.description: The binary frame structure used by WebSockets to encapsulate messages with headers and payloads.

concepts.name: websocket-upgrade-handshake

concepts.name: broadcasting-messages
concepts.description: Sending a message frame to all connected clients efficiently with backpressure and error handling.

concepts.name: client-registry
concepts.description: A Map storing client records with id, socket, name, rooms, lastSeen, and isAlive for managing connected clients.

concepts.name: connection-state-machine
concepts.description: A TCP socket connection transitions through handshake and open states to handle WebSocket upgrade and frames.

concepts.name: message-fan-out
concepts.description: Publishing a message to all members of a room efficiently by encoding once and writing to each client's socket.

concepts.name: rooms-and-channels
concepts.description: Rooms are named channels where clients subscribe to receive messages, enabling scoped publish-subscribe communication.

concepts.name: subscribe-and-unsubscribe
concepts.description: Clients join or leave rooms with idempotent operations that update membership indexes and handle edge cases.

concepts.name: application-level-heartbeats
concepts.description: Heartbeats sent at the application layer to detect dead peers and keep connections alive through intermediaries.

concepts.name: idle-status-detection
concepts.description: Determining user idle status by tracking last active time separate from last pong to avoid false activity.

concepts.name: ping-pong-protocol
concepts.description: WebSocket control frames ping (0x9) and pong (0xA) used to check connection liveness and echo payloads.

concepts.name: presence-list
concepts.description: A computed list of users currently online in a room, grouped by user and updated with status and activity.

concepts.name: in-memory-pub-sub-limitation
concepts.description: In-memory pub/sub only works within a single process and cannot scale across multiple server processes.

concepts.name: message-broker
concepts.description: A message broker enables communication and message fan-out between multiple server processes to scale pub/sub systems.

concepts.name: redis-pub-sub
concepts.description: Redis pub/sub is a fire-and-forget messaging system that broadcasts messages to subscribers without persistence or replay.

concepts.name: redis-streams
concepts.description: Redis Streams provide a durable, ordered log of messages supporting history, replay, and reliable delivery with consumer groups.

concepts.name: load-balancing-algorithms-for-websockets
concepts.description: Using least_conn or ip_hash algorithms in load balancers to distribute WebSocket connections effectively.

concepts.name: nginx-websocket-proxying
concepts.description: Configuring nginx to correctly proxy WebSocket connections by forwarding Upgrade headers and using HTTP/1.1.

concepts.name: redis-presence-management
concepts.description: Using Redis sorted sets with timestamps to track and expire user presence across multiple server processes.

concepts.name: redis-pub-sub-for-presence
concepts.description: Servers publish presence change events on Redis channels to synchronize presence snapshots across processes.

concepts.name: sticky-sessions
concepts.description: Sticky sessions ensure a client consistently connects to the same backend server to maintain session state.

concepts.name: abstract-syntax-tree
concepts.description: A tree representation of source code structure built from tokens during parsing.

concepts.name: bytecode
concepts.description: A compact list of simple instructions produced by the interpreter from the AST for execution.
lectures: 1.2 - From Source Text to Running Code

concepts.name: call-stack
concepts.description: A last-in, first-out stack of execution contexts tracking currently running code.
lectures: 1.3 - Execution Contexts and the Call Stack

concepts.name: execution-context
concepts.description: A record created when code runs, holding scope, this value, and return position information.
lectures: 1.3 - Execution Contexts and the Call Stack

concepts.name: tokenizer
concepts.description: A tool that splits source code text into meaningful tokens for parsing.
lectures: 1.2 - From Source Text to Running Code

concepts.name: closure

concepts.name: hoisting
concepts.description: Declarations are created before code runs with different initialization states, explaining variable behavior.

concepts.name: lexical-scope
concepts.description: Scope is determined by the physical location of code, not by where functions are called.

concepts.name: scope-chain
concepts.description: A linked chain of scopes where variable lookup searches outward from inner to outer scopes.
lectures: 2.1 - Lexical Scope and the Scope Chain

concepts.name: temporal-dead-zone
concepts.description: The period from scope start until let/const declarations are initialized where accessing them throws ReferenceError.

concepts.name: arrow-function-this

concepts.name: constructor-functions

concepts.name: this-binding-rules
concepts.description: The four rules determining how the this keyword is bound based on call site: default, implicit, explicit, and new binding.
lectures: 3.1 - How this Gets Bound: The Four Rules

concepts.name: class-inheritance-links
concepts.description: The class extends syntax sets up prototype links for instances and static methods to enable inheritance.

concepts.name: class-syntax-sugar
concepts.description: The `class` keyword is syntactic sugar over the same prototype chain — Dog.prototype gets Animal.prototype as its prototype.

concepts.name: instanceof-operator-implementation
concepts.description: The instanceof operator checks if a constructor's prototype exists anywhere in an object's prototype chain.

concepts.name: object-create-polyfill

concepts.name: prototype-delegation
concepts.description: Objects delegate property lookups to their prototype rather than copying properties, enabling shared methods and memory efficiency.

concepts.name: prototype-inheritance
concepts.description: Every object has an internal link to another object, its prototype, and property lookups walk that chain.

concepts.name: prototype-lookup
concepts.description: The process of walking an object's prototype chain to find a property if not found directly on the object.

concepts.name: hidden-class-transitions
concepts.description: Adding properties in different orders creates new hidden classes, causing transitions that affect performance.

concepts.name: inline-caches
concepts.description: V8 caches property offsets at each access site keyed by hidden class to speed up repeated property access.

concepts.name: monomorphic-polymorphic-megamorphic
concepts.description: Inline caches can be monomorphic (one shape), polymorphic (few shapes), or megamorphic (many shapes), affecting performance.

concepts.name: v8-hidden-classes
concepts.description: V8 creates an internal hidden class describing an object's shape; adding properties in a different order produces a different hidden class.

concepts.name: async-await-mechanism
concepts.description: Async/await syntax is syntactic sugar for promise chains using microtasks to schedule continuations.

concepts.name: event-loop
concepts.description: A single call stack plus a macrotask queue (setTimeout, etc.) — the next macrotask runs once the stack empties.

concepts.name: event-loop-simulator
concepts.description: A programmatic model of the event loop with macrotask and microtask queues and a fake clock for deterministic testing.

concepts.name: macrotask-queue
concepts.description: A queue holding callbacks from timers, I/O, and DOM events, run one at a time when the call stack is empty.

concepts.name: microtask-queue
concepts.description: Promises resolve into a separate, higher-priority microtask queue that fully drains before the next macrotask runs.

concepts.name: closure-scope-bug
concepts.description: A bug caused by closures capturing a single shared variable in a loop due to var scoping, leading to unexpected values.

concepts.name: hidden-class-polymorphism
concepts.description: Objects with varying property shapes cause polymorphic hidden classes, impacting performance due to shape transitions.

concepts.name: layered-debugging
concepts.description: A method of debugging by analyzing program behavior through different conceptual layers to identify root causes.

concepts.name: run-to-completion-rule

concepts.name: request-response-contract

concepts.name: websocket-api
concepts.description: The browser API for creating and managing WebSocket connections with events and message handling.

concepts.name: websocket-frames
concepts.description: Data is sent in frames with opcodes and masking to enable efficient full-duplex communication.

concepts.name: websocket-handshake
concepts.description: The server answers 101 Switching Protocols with a Sec-WebSocket-Accept derived from the client's key, after which the connection is full-duplex.

concepts.name: polling-vs-websockets
concepts.description: Long-polling pays a full HTTP request per message with a reconnect gap; a WebSocket keeps one long-lived full-duplex connection with tiny framing overhead.

concepts.name: server-sent-events
concepts.description: A one-way server-to-client push over HTTP using a persistent text stream and automatic reconnection.

concepts.name: transport-measurements
concepts.description: Measuring bytes, latency, and open connections to compare efficiency of real-time transport methods.
lectures: 3.3 - Measuring the Cost: Bytes, Latency and Open Connections

concepts.name: websockets
concepts.description: A persistent, full-duplex TCP connection established via HTTP Upgrade for efficient bidirectional communication.
lectures: 5.1 - Shipping the Scoreboard: One Transport per Feature

concepts.name: backpressure
concepts.description: A condition where the sender produces data faster than the receiver can consume, causing buffers to fill.

concepts.name: bufferedamount
concepts.description: A WebSocket property indicating the number of bytes queued but not yet sent over the network.

concepts.name: exponential-backoff
concepts.description: A reconnection strategy that doubles the wait time after each failure, up to a maximum, to reduce server overload.

concepts.name: heartbeat

concepts.name: commit-phase
concepts.description: The phase where React compares the new UI description with the old and updates the DOM accordingly.

concepts.name: re-render-triggers
concepts.description: The specific events that cause React to re-render a component: state changes, context changes, and parent re-renders.

concepts.name: reference-stability
concepts.description: Keeping the same object or function references across renders to prevent unnecessary re-renders.

concepts.name: render-phase
concepts.description: The phase where React calls a component function to compute the UI description without touching the DOM.
lectures: 1.2 - Render vs Commit: What React Actually Does

concepts.name: commit-chart
concepts.description: A visual timeline showing React commit durations and frequency during profiling.
lectures: 2.1 - Profiling the Dashboard with React DevTools

concepts.name: flame-graph
concepts.description: A component tree visualization showing render times and reasons for each component in a commit.
lectures: 2.1 - Profiling the Dashboard with React DevTools

concepts.name: react-devtools-profiler
concepts.description: A tool to record and analyze React component renders and commits to measure performance.

concepts.name: render-cost-analysis
concepts.description: Evaluating render times and frequency to prioritize performance fixes effectively.
lectures: 2.2 - Reading the Flame Graph for Wasted Renders

concepts.name: wasted-render

concepts.name: computed-state
concepts.description: State derived from props or other state values that can be memoized to prevent redundant recalculations.

concepts.name: lifting-content-up
concepts.description: Passing expensive children as props to a stateful wrapper to keep children references stable and skip re-renders.
lectures: 3.1 - Moving State Down and Lifting Content Up

concepts.name: memoization
concepts.description: Caching the result of an expensive computation to avoid recomputing when inputs haven't changed.

concepts.name: moving-state-down
concepts.description: Placing state in the component that directly uses it to limit re-renders to smaller subtrees.
lectures: 3.1 - Moving State Down and Lifting Content Up

concepts.name: use-memo
concepts.description: useMemo memoizes a computed value and only recomputes it when its dependencies change.

concepts.name: usememo-overhead
concepts.description: The performance cost of useMemo from dependency comparisons and bookkeeping, which can outweigh benefits if misused.
lectures: 3.3 - When useMemo Costs More Than It Saves

concepts.name: context-re-render-storm
concepts.description: Context updates cause all consumers to re-render regardless of React.memo, leading to re-render storms when context values change frequently.
lectures: 4.3 - Splitting Context to Stop Re-render Storms

concepts.name: inline-objects-and-functions
concepts.description: Inline objects, arrays, and functions passed as props create new references each render, breaking React.memo optimizations.

concepts.name: react-memo
concepts.description: React.memo skips a component's re-render when its props are shallowly equal to the previous render.

concepts.name: shallow-equality
concepts.description: Primitives compare by value; objects, arrays, and functions compare by reference.

concepts.name: splitting-context
concepts.description: Splitting context into smaller focused contexts and memoizing provider values reduces unnecessary re-renders caused by context updates.
lectures: 4.3 - Splitting Context to Stop Re-render Storms

concepts.name: use-callback
concepts.description: useCallback keeps a function reference stable across renders as long as its dependencies don't change.

concepts.name: use-deferred-value

concepts.name: use-transition
concepts.description: A React hook to mark state updates as low priority, allowing urgent updates to interrupt and keep UI responsive.
lectures: 5.2 - useTransition and useDeferredValue for Lag-Free Filtering

concepts.name: virtualization
concepts.description: Rendering only visible rows plus a buffer to reduce DOM nodes and improve performance in large lists.

concepts.name: windowing
concepts.description: Another term for virtualization, focusing on rendering a window of visible items in a scrollable list.

concepts.name: memo-boundary-complexity
concepts.description: The added maintenance cost and complexity from using memoization techniques like dependency arrays and split contexts.
lectures: 6.1 - Before and After: Profiling the Fixed Dashboard

concepts.name: performance-budget
concepts.description: A target time threshold per interaction to maintain responsive UI and monitor performance regressions.
lectures: 6.1 - Before and After: Profiling the Fixed Dashboard

concepts.name: profiling-workflow
concepts.description: A systematic process of measuring baseline, hypothesizing, changing one thing, and measuring again to optimize performance.
